chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from his men, from Yūnus, from them, peace be upon them, who said:

If you intend to perform the ghusl (ritual washing) of the dead person, then place him upon the washing place facing the qiblah. If he is wearing a shirt, then bring his hand out from the shirt, and place his shirt over his private parts, and raise them from his legs to above the knees. If he is not wearing a shirt, then cast a cloth over his private parts. Then proceed to the lote leaves, put them in a basin, pour water over them, and beat them with your hand until their foam rises. Set aside the foam in something, and pour the remainder into the large washing vessel that contains the water. Then wash his hand three times, as a person washes from janabah, up to the middle of the forearm, and wash his private part and cleanse it. Then wash his head with the foam, and go to excess in that, and strive that water does not enter his nostrils and his ears. Then lay him on his left side and pour water from half of his head to his feet three times, and rub his body with gentle rubbing, and likewise his back and his belly. Then lay him on his right side and do to him the like of that. Then pour out that water from the vessel, wash the vessel with pure water, and wash your hands up to the elbows. Then pour water into the container, cast into it some grains of camphor, and do with him as you did in the first time: begin with his hands, then his private part, and wipe his belly with a gentle wiping; if something comes out, then cleanse it. Then wash his head, then lay him on his left side as you did the first time. Then wash your hand up to the elbows and the container, and pour into it pure water, and wash him with pure water just as you washed in the first two times. Then dry him with a pure garment, and proceed to cotton, sprinkle upon it some hanut, and place it upon his private part, front and rear, and stuff the cotton into his anus so that nothing may come out from it. Take a long strip of cloth, its width being a span, and tie it from his loins, press his thighs together firmly, and wrap them in his thighs. Then bring out its head from beneath his legs to the right side, and tuck it into the place in which you wrapped the cloth. And the cloth should be long, wrapping his thighs from his loins to his knees with a firm wrapping.
As for what he mentioned within the course of that, regarding giving precedence to the wudu (ablution) of the dead person before his ghusl, then that indicates it.

key_terms.السِّدْرِ: lote leaves used in the first washing of the deceased
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction the deceased is to be faced toward during washing
key_terms.حَنُوطٍ: perfuming substance applied to the deceased
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهِ: the private parts that must be covered during the procedure
key_terms.غُسْلَ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.كَافُورٍ: camphor placed in the water for one of the washings
key_terms.مَاءَ الْقَرَاحِ: plain pure water used in the final washing
key_terms.وُضُوءِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ablution of the deceased before the ritual washing

ai.seo_question: How is the ghusl of a deceased person performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the detailed procedure for the ghusl (ritual washing) of the deceased, including covering the 'awrah, using lote leaves and camphor, the sequence of washing, and preparing the body afterward. It also indicates the precedence of wudu (ablution) for the deceased before the ghusl, making it a key jurisprudential text on funeral rites in Shia fiqh.
